title: Cold-start SDKenV Waiting Room playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for a lightweight ‘waiting room’ pattern for SDK-powered apps to reduce cold-start latency and noisy first requests. Target audience: developer-experience engineers, SDK maintainers, solutions engineers running pilots, and SRE on-call for early rollouts.

Summary / problem statement:
- Many first requests to the Redwood hosted API (or Dedicated pools) from freshly-started client processes show 200-600ms extra latency due to: model cold caches, initial kernel/path selection, and occasional GPU context warming.
- For short-lived environments (CI, microservices with bursty containers, serverless functions), this causes bad first-user experiences and noisy telemetry that skews SLA calculations.
- We want an SDK-side pattern that:
  * Keeps the UX simple (opt-in toggle),
  * Requires minimal infra changes on Redwood side,
  * Can be used both by quickstarts and by real customer apps during deploys.

Hypothesis:
Implementing an ephemeral ‘waiting room’ in the SDK (small warmup queue + probe requests + KV-prefetch) will reduce p50/p95 of first meaningful token latencies by >25% for cold processes without increasing cost significantly.

Design sketch (waiting-room flow):
1) SDK initialization (opt-in flag: waiting_room.enabled = true)
   - Create lightweight background worker thread (or async task) that holds a small FIFO queue of warmup tasks.

2) Warmup tasks (recipes):
   - micro-probe: 1-3 no-op token-generation calls with minimal sequence length to trigger model path selection and kernel warm-up.
   - prompt-prefetch: send a short seeded prompt that exercises common decoding paths + function-calling stub if app enables it.
   - kv-prefill: for chat-style apps, prefill a small KV cache by replaying a single user-turn from a canned sample.

3) Admission / pacing:
   - Only run warmups while queue length < N (default N=2) and worker CPU < threshold.
   - Exponential backoff if the backend responds with throttle or error.

4) Visibility:
   - SDK emits telemetry events: waiting_room.started, waiting_room.probe_ok, waiting_room.probe_failed, waiting_room.finished.
   - Emit metrics (tagged): warmup_delta_ms (difference in average token latency pre/post warmup), warmup_cost_tokens, warmup_errors.

Experiment matrix (first-pass):
- Variables: probe type (noop vs seeded prompt), probe count (1,3), KV prefill enabled (yes/no), parallel warmup limit (1,2,4), warmup timeout (500ms, 1500ms, 5000ms).
- Metrics: first-request p50/p95 latency, tokens used per warmup, error rate on first 100 requests, customer-visible error rate (status != 200), cold-run percentile improvements.
- Environments: Hosted API (small testing pool), Dedicated small pool, and Private deployments in our staging VPC.

Quickstart (developer-facing, 15m):
- Goal: show how to opt into the waiting room locally and measure impact.
- Steps:
  1) pip/npm/yarn install redwood-sdk@waitroom-preview (local artifact or feature flag).
  2) Set env: REDWOOD_WAITING_ROOM=1; REDWOOD_WAIT_ROOM_MAX=2
  3) Start the sample app: examples/waiting-room/sample-chat.js
  4) Run ./scripts/emit-requests.sh  --first-run only
  5) Check logs: waiting_room.started and waiting_room.finished (look for warmup_delta_ms tag)
  6) Compare run with and without waiting room using scripts/compare-latency.py

Warmup recipes (code pseudocode):
- micro_probe():
    call client.generate({ model: default, prompt: "" , max_tokens: 1, stream: false })
- seeded_probe():
    call client.generate({ model: default, prompt: sample_prompt(), temperature: 0.0, max_tokens: 4 })
- kv_prefill(chat_sample):
    call client.chat.append(chat_sample) // internal, small footprint

Runbook and safety checks:
- If waiting_room.probe_failed occurs more than 5x in 10 minutes -> disable waiting room automatically and emit alert to SRE via slack:#sre-sdk-warmup.
- Cost guardrail: do not warm more than K tokens per process lifetime (default K=200).
- Privacy: probes must never include customer PII. Use canned prompts stored in SDK.
- Fallback behavior: if backend returns capacity-fallback code, mark waiting room disabled for 1 minute and route normal calls through existing retry/backoff logic.

Telemetry & dashboards:
- New Grafana dashboard: "SDK Waiting Room" with panels for warmup success rate, avg warmup tokens, first-request latency delta, per-region breakdown.
- Split tags by customer-tier: hosted/free, hosted-paid, dedicated.
- Example alert: p95 first-request latency increased by 40% vs baseline and warmup_success_rate < 60% -> page eng-sdks on-call.

Backwards compatibility / opt-in strategy:
- Default OFF. Expose: REDWOOD_WAITING_ROOM=1 and client config waiting_room: { enabled: true, mode: "aggressive|conservative" }.
- Conservative mode: run only seeded_probe once if process idle for 200ms after init.
- Aggressive mode: run up to 3 probes immediately after init.

Lab checklist (to run before a pilot):
- [ ] Implement telemetry events and sample logs in local dev.
- [ ] Add warmup token accounting to billing simulation script.
- [ ] Run A/B test on internal infra: 1000 cold containers vs 1000 warm containers.
- [ ] Validate Private deployment behavior in staging VPC (no external outbound if customer policy denies it).
- [ ] Draft SDK docs + quickstart (short copy for README + one-liner).

Open questions & tradeoffs (notes-to-self):
- Do customers want this behavior baked into the server side instead? Pro: centralized logic, Pro: fewer duplicate probes across many clients. Con: more infra complexity and potentially extra cost. Link to Confluence note for server-side tradeoffs.
- How will waiting-room interact with model rollouts/variant selection? Need to ensure probes exercise the same model variant the app will use.
- Should we add a small keepalive ping API that is cheaper than generation calls? (Discuss with runtime team)

Next steps (owner: Evelyn):
1) Prototype micro_probe flow in branch feature/waiting-room-proto (PR created: see linked_artifacts).
2) Add instrumentation hooks and a minimal dashboard prototype (owner: Leo).
3) Run smoke A/B in hosted-internal pool and post results by 2025-03-15.

Related threads: slack:#devexp-sdk-wg (see thread ts=1678392000), jira REINF-458 (load-test request), confluence page (linked_artifacts).

Appendix: sample canned prompts (must be non-sensitive):
- "Summarize in 1 sentence: the quickstart SDK waiting-room warmup."
- "Return OK" (a deterministic short response stub)

Notes (informal):
- This is a sketch — keep it lightweight for initial rollout. Try to keep changes in SDK surface minimal.
- If we see warmup tokens consistently hitting billing thresholds for large fleets, pivot to server-side keepalive.
- Remember to cross-post final playbook to shared_drives/product/hosted-api when stable.

-- Evelyn
